question.text: What is the current status of entry load in Indian mutual funds?

answer.text: Entry load is no longer permitted; the sale price of open-ended scheme units equals the applicable NAV
Entry load of 2.25% is permitted for equity schemes
Entry load is optional and can be charged at the discretion of the AMC
Entry load of 1% is mandatory for all mutual fund schemes

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series V-A workbook (pp.150-151, 170), entry load is no longer permitted by SEBI for mutual fund schemes. As a result, the sale price of open-ended scheme units equals the applicable NAV — the formula effectively reduces to Sale Price = NAV + 0 = NAV. Page 170 reiterates that the ongoing sale price equals the applicable NAV because entry load is not permitted. The Trap: 2.25% was a pre-abolition equity entry load and is outdated. Entry load is neither optional/discretionary nor mandatory at any level — it is simply not permitted. The keyed answer deliberately avoids citing a specific effective date because that detail was not found on the pages checked (pp.150, 151, 170). Note: Following the abolition of entry load, SEBI allowed AMCs to use a portion of TER to pay distributor commissions. This shifted distributor compensation from a one-time upfront charge to an ongoing trail-commission model funded from the scheme's TER.
